requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST supply the review prompt that each group's reviewer follows. The prompt MUST direct the reviewer not to edit files. It MUST direct the reviewer to make mechanical changes itself in the revised text it returns, and to return design questions for the user.
rationale:
The requirement has three obligations. The `habeas-requirements` skill supplies the review prompt. The prompt directs the reviewer not to edit files. The prompt directs the reviewer to make mechanical changes itself in the revised text and to return design questions for the user.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_makes_mechanical_changes_and_returns_design_questions]` covers all three:

- **Supply:** The test loads the prompt through `review_prompt()`. That helper calls `skill_file("habeas-requirements", "references/review-prompt.md")`, so the test fails if the skill doesn't ship this prompt. I did not read `skill_file`; I took the supply check from its name and the arguments `review_prompt()` passes.
- **No file edits:** The test asserts the whitespace-collapsed prompt contains "Don't edit files; make your changes in the revised text you return". The helpers `collapse` and `assert_text` make this a real check. `collapse` joins whitespace so line wraps don't hide a phrase. `assert_text` panics if any phrase is missing.
- **Mechanical changes made by the reviewer:** The test asserts "**Mechanical changes:** make them yourself in the revised text, and never phrase them as questions".
- **Design questions returned:** The test asserts "**Design questions:** return these; the user decides".

I read `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md`. It contains these exact directives, and its "Two kinds of finding" section is consistent with the requirement.

The requirement has no boundary or failure cases beyond these directives. Checking that the prompt text contains them is the appropriate test for a prompt-content requirement. I found no plausible violation that would pass: removing or changing any of the three directives would fail the assertions.
